title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Substring Operation
summary: Given a string s made of lowercase English letters, choose any non-empty substring and replace each letter with the one before it in the alphabet.
statement: Given a string s made of lowercase English letters, choose any non-empty substring and replace each letter with the one before it in the alphabet. Output the lexicographically smallest string achievable through this operation.
constraints: Replace each chosen character by its alphabet predecessor, with a wrapping to z.
Return the lexicographically smallest string obtainable.
hints: Avoid decrementing a because it wraps to z, except when every character is a.
Start at the first non-a character and decrement its maximal consecutive non-a block.
If no such character exists, replace only the final a with z.
The earliest improvable position dominates lexicographic order; extending through non-a characters improves the string until the first harmful wrap.
editorial: The earliest improvable position dominates lexicographic order; extending through non-a characters improves the string until the first harmful wrap.

tests.explanation: Decrement the initial cb to ba; stopping before a avoids wrapping it to z, producing baabc.
Every choice wraps selected a characters to z, so changing only the last gives aaaz.
